summary: Independent TER falsification found no new locked-methodology blocker. Primary filings confirm meaningful customer concentration and robotics execution risk, while the 2026 proxy shows conventional governance controls and performance-linked compensation. These risks should remain explicit in the packet; they do not justify manufacturing a blocker. Alpha's remaining governance/equity-plan normalization gate is not duplicated here.

claims.claim: The strongest present red-team challenge is concentration: one direct customer represented 19% of 2025 consolidated revenue and two specifying customers drove 12% and 10%, creating material platform/customer dependency.

Robotics execution is a genuine contradiction to a frictionless diversification narrative because prior filings disclosed macro pressure, leadership changes and a quarterly loss during channel transformation.

The 2026 proxy reports eight of nine directors independent and discloses anti-hedging/pledging, ownership and performance-linked compensation controls; no primary-source governance fact reviewed here supports escalating governance itself into a Beta blocker.

risks: Large-customer platform decisions can produce nonlinear revenue loss.
Semiconductor test demand remains cyclical despite AI-related strength.
Robotics turnaround/channel transformation may consume time and management attention without delivering diversification economics.
contradictions: Diversification narrative vs disclosed robotics losses/transition risk.
Broad secular test thesis vs material dependence on a few specifying/purchasing customers.
unknowns: Current crowding/valuation expectations are non-canonical and intentionally not promoted into Earth Score.
Future competitive platform wins/losses remain unknown until observable.
